changes.current_line: Financial infrastructure to grow globally, in every currency.
changes.change: For regional subscription businesses (e.g. a US and Canada membership chain), open with: "Send us one month of failed renewals and we'll show you which ones would have come back." Run that data session as the lead pitch, ahead of any platform or global-reach story.
changes.why: The global opener drew silence from a two-country chain, while the export of their own failed renewals got the silent controller to ask for the spreadsheet, and the deal was signed four days later.

changes.current_line: Recover failed payments automatically with smart retries.
changes.change: For subscription and membership businesses: "Some of your churn is members who never meant to leave. Split the people who cancelled from the people whose card just failed, and we'll win back the second group automatically." Do not attach a share-of-churn figure until we have a verified one.
changes.why: The customer framed the problem as splitting cancellations from failed cards, found the failed-card group was bigger than expected, and described those customers as 'members who never meant to leave'; recovery was the element they reacted to. That framing is sharper than our generic retry claim.

changes.current_line: Online and in-store on one platform; the line between them has pretty much disappeared.
changes.change: For customers running front desks on third-party studio or vertical management software: "Online membership billing runs on us today. Front-desk payments inside your studio software run through our partner integration, and we'll show you that flow in your own setup." Do not claim the line between online and in-store has disappeared until we can demo it live in their software.
changes.why: The customer asked to see our reader working inside their studio software and we could not show it live, because it depends on a partner integration. The front desk remains unsigned and still sits with the incumbent.

changes.change: Add a finance-facing proof point for the controller or whoever signs: state our contract term and termination costs plainly, and set them against an incumbent counter of a rate review plus a terminal bundle on a longer contract. Bring it to the first meeting that includes the signer rather than leaving it to the champion.
changes.why: The incumbent countered with a hardware bundle on a longer contract, the controller asked about termination fees twice, and the paper sat with him for two weeks before he signed. Switching cost was the signer's concern, and our library has no line that answers it.
